questions.question: What are zero values in Go, and how do they work?
questions.title: Go basic types and zero values: meaning and behaviour
questions.direct_answer: Every variable in Go has a defined value even when no explicit initializer is written. Numbers start at `0`, booleans at `false`, strings at an empty string, and pointers, slices, maps, channels, functions, and interfaces at `nil`. Arrays and structs are zeroed recursively. Good Go types often make their zero value useful, but `nil` reference-like values do not all behave the same way.
